workload: three interactive browser tasks, run back to back by a script

findings.caching_works: caching removes 54% of input spend versus sending the same traffic uncached
findings.MIN-1: 4 requests place a cache marker on a prefix of ~810 tokens against a 4,096 minimum; all returned creation=0 and read=0
findings.no_1h_path: confirmed on 0.13.7: the Anthropic serializer emits ephemeral with no ttl key anywhere

conclusion: The 1-hour TTL hypothesis does not apply to this workload. Median gap 7.3s, zero of 26 gaps in the 5m-1h band. At this cadence a 5-minute entry never expires between requests, so a 1h write at 2x would cost more than the 1.25x it replaces.
limits: A short automated run of back-to-back tasks. It says nothing about a deployment whose cadence is human-paced or scheduled, which is the case the hypothesis was about.
